chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who separates from his wife without divorce or an oath, for a year, not approaching her bed. He said to me: Let him come to her family.

He said: Whichever man makes an oath of abstention from his wife, and al-i'la' is that he says: 'By Allah, I will not have sexual intercourse with you for such and such a period,' and says: 'By Allah, I will annoy you,' so he angers her, then he is given a respite of four months.
Then after the four months he is taken and held in suspense. If he returns (fulfills), and al-ifa' is that he reconciles with his family, then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

And if he does not return, compulsion for divorce is applied, and a divorce does not take place between them until he is held in suspense. And it is also after the four months that he is compelled to either return or be divorced.

key_terms.إِيلَاء: Oath of abstention from sexual relations with one's wife
key_terms.فَاءَ: To return or repent from the oath
key_terms.يَهْجُرُ: To separate or turn away from
key_terms.يُوقَفُ: To be held in suspense or suspended status

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and procedure for Ila (oath of abstention) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the procedural mechanics of 'Ila', distinguishing it from simple separation by mandating a four-month suspension period where the husband is legally held in abeyance. It emphasizes that the divorce is not automatic but requires judicial intervention to compel either reconciliation or formal divorce if the oath is broken, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preventing hasty dissolution of marriage. The text also highlights the spiritual dimension, noting that if the husband repents and resumes relations, it is considered a form of reconciliation under God's mercy.
